context:
Start from the trace, not from guesswork. The suite already captures
traces on failure - the first step is to confirm whether the failing
step is a WASM download, an `ATTACH`, or a navigation. Pick the
remediation that addresses that specific step.
description:
The browser-functional suite added by
`implement-results-explorer-browser-functional-tests` has Chromium as a
blocking gate and Firefox + WebKit `@smoke` as non-blocking
cross-browser coverage.

Root cause (confirmed w1): under default Playwright parallelism (5 workers),
all 8 `@smoke` tests navigate to different routes simultaneously. Each page
independently instantiates a DuckDB-WASM worker; WebKit serializes WASM
compilation differently from Chromium/Firefox and stalls past the 10 s
`expect` timeout when multiple pages compete for init. Moving DuckDB-WASM
to same-origin bundled assets did NOT retire the flake - the race is WASM
init contention, not CDN latency.

Fix applied (w2): `--workers=1` added to the `test:e2e:webkit` npm script
and to the `test:e2e:full` inline webkit invocation, serializing init so
each test page gets an uncontested WASM worker. Chromium and Firefox are
unaffected. 8/8 pass on 3 consecutive local runs.

Remaining work (w3): accumulate 10 consecutive CI green runs, then promote
WebKit from `continue-on-error: true` to a blocking gate.

anti_patterns.instead: graduate it once stable, don't remove it.
anti_patterns.why: Safari/WebKit rendering is a real user surface

anti_patterns.dont: flip `continue-on-error: true` off on a calendar / release schedule
anti_patterns.instead: gate the flip on the 10-consecutive-green criterion in w3 and nothing else.
anti_patterns.why: promoting WebKit before the flake is actually fixed will regress main

anti_patterns.dont: paper over the flake with retries
anti_patterns.instead: identify and fix the root cause.
anti_patterns.why: this hides the underlying WebKit-specific issue and ships silent instability to maintainers

preserves.behavior: No production-code seam is introduced for failure injection - the original architecture decision stands.
The Chromium blocking gate continues to run the full suite without regression.

work_units.notes:
Reproduced: default parallelism (5 workers) → 4/8 failed. Pattern: `waitForShell`
passes (nav link renders) but page-specific headings time out within 10 s.
Root cause: concurrent DuckDB-WASM worker startup stalls in WebKit when
multiple pages initialize simultaneously. Same-origin bundled assets did NOT
retire the flake - race is WASM init contention, not CDN latency.

work_units.notes:
Fix applied: added `--workers=1` to the `test:e2e:webkit` npm script so WebKit
tests run serially (one DuckDB-WASM init at a time). Added explanatory comment
to playwright.config.ts webkit project block. Chromium and Firefox unaffected.
Verified 8/8 pass on 3 consecutive clean local runs.
